meta.titre: Using context clues to fill vocabulary gaps

sections.contenu_markdown: Filling a gap correctly means reading beyond the blank itself: the words before and after it often carry the real clue.

Filling gaps in a passage requires reading the whole sentence (and often the surrounding sentences) to identify grammatical clues (singular/plural, verb agreement, preposition) and semantic clues (which word logically fits the meaning), rather than matching words in isolation.

sections.enonce_markdown: Fill the gap: 'Machinery has already replaced large numbers of workers in many ___.' (choices include: factories, laboratories, researches)

etapes.justification: The blank follows 'many', requiring a plural countable noun.
Machinery replacing workers happens in places of production.

sections.conclusion_markdown: "Machinery has already replaced large numbers of workers in many factories."

items.erreur_markdown: Choosing a word based only on its general theme (technology-related) without checking grammatical fit (singular/plural, part of speech).
items.pourquoi_faux: A word can be thematically related but grammatically wrong (e.g. an uncountable noun where a plural is required); both clues must be checked together.
items.correction_markdown: Always verify both the grammatical form and the meaning before finalising a gap-fill answer.

items.enonce_markdown: Fill the gap: 'Scientists carry out important ___.' (experiments / experiment)
items.solution_markdown: experiments (plural, matching the general/plural context of ongoing scientific activity).

items_markdown: Read the whole sentence, not just the immediate words around the gap
Check grammatical clues (number, part of speech) and semantic clues together
